item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 300506
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sat Aug 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located
well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of disturbed weather, associated with a tropical wave, is
located well to the south of southwestern Mexico. This system is
expected to move west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15
mph. Environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual
development of this system, and a tropical depression is likely to
form during the early to middle part of next week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in the next few days. Some gradual development is
possible thereafter while it moves slowly westward across the
central Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

Hurricane Karina Advisory Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026
 
...KARINA BECOMES A HURRICANE...
...EXPECTED TO CONTINUE TO GAIN STRENGTH...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.3N 121.1W
ABOUT 820 MI...1325 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...80 MPH...130 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...980 MB...28.94 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located
near latitude 17.3 North, longitude 121.1 West. Karina is moving
toward the west-northwest near 15 mph (24 km/h). A slower westward
to west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 80 mph (130 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Steady to rapid strengthening seems likely, and Karina is 
forecast to become a major hurricane in a day or so.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles
(370 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 980 mb (28.94 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Karina will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
couple of days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening
surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your
local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 300832
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 AM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026
 
Satellite images indicate that Karina is strengthening and has 
become a hurricane. Curved bands now wrap completely around the 
center, and the dry slots noted earlier have filled in. There is a 
wide range in the latest satellite intensity estimates, from about 
50 to 80 kt. The initial intensity is increased to 70 kt, based on 
a blend of the estimates and continued improved cloud pattern. A 
partial ASCAT pass indicates that the wind field has contracted, and 
the initial 34- and 50-kt wind radii have been updated based on 
that data.
 
Now that Karina has a closed and symmetric inner core, significant 
strengthening seems likely given that the hurricane is forecast to 
remain in conducive environmental conditions for the next couple of 
days. The strengthening process is expected to stall on Monday, 
followed by a gradual weakening trend as Karina moves over 
progressively cooler waters and into a drier airmass during the 
middle and latter portions of the week. The NHC intensity forecast 
is higher than the previous one, but still below the GDMI and HCCA 
aids.
 
The hurricane is moving west-northwestward at about 13 kt. The high
pressure system to the north of Karina is expected to weaken due to
an amplifying trough over the western U.S. However, there should be
enough ridging to keep Karina on a westward to west-northwestward
course, albeit at a slower pace, throughout the week. There is a
fair amount of spread in the model guidance from days 3 to 5, but in
general, the latest models have shifted southward this cycle. Based
on this guidance, the NHC track forecast has been nudged southward,
but still lies on the northern side of the guidance envelope.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lowell Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sat Aug 29 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 300232
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Lowell Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP122026
500 PM HST Sat Aug 29 2026
 
Lowell's convective organization has changed little during the past 
several hours. Moderate easterly vertical wind shear continues to 
displace the bulk of the deep convection over and west of the 
low-level circulation center. Based on a blend of an earlier 
scatterometer pass, the latest objective intensity estimates, and 
the subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB, the initial 
intensity is raised to 45 kt for this advisory.

Lowell is moving westward, or 270/8 kt. A low- to mid-level ridge 
positioned north of the cyclone should remain the primary steering 
influence during the next couple of days, resulting in a continued 
westward motion. The track guidance is in generally good agreement 
during this period. Thereafter, considerable cross-track spread 
develops in the guidance, likely due in part to the potential 
influence of Tropical Storm Karina on Lowell's steering flow. The 
latest HCCA and Google DeepMind ensemble mean have shifted slightly 
southward and maintain a generally westward motion, while the GFS, 
regional hurricane models, and simple consensus (TVCN) support a 
gradual west-northwestward to northwestward turn later in the 
forecast period. Given the considerable spread among these 
solutions, the latest NHC track forecast reflects a blend of the 
previous forecast, HCCA, and Google DeepMind ensemble mean, and has 
been nudged slightly southward from the previous advisory.

The moderate easterly vertical wind shear affecting Lowell is 
forecast to persist in the short term, which should temper the rate 
of strengthening. However, the shear is expected to gradually 
decrease during the next day or two while Lowell remains over warm 
waters, which should allow the cyclone to become better organized 
and gradually strengthen. Environmental conditions are forecast to 
become more favorable thereafter, with very low vertical wind shear 
expected by early next week, and a faster rate of strengthening is 
anticipated. The intensity forecast becomes increasingly uncertain 
later in the period due to Lowell's potential interaction with 
Karina. The current forecast track keeps the cyclones sufficiently 
separated for Lowell to continue strengthening, while a slower and 
more northwestward solution could expose Lowell to stronger shear 
associated with outflow from Karina and result in a weaker cyclone. 
The latest NHC intensity forecast is essentially unchanged from 
the previous advisory and remains near the middle of the guidance 
envelope.
